items.name_local: Studiefinanciering (basisbeurs, aanvullende beurs, rentedragende lening) — burgers EU/EER, Zwitserland of VK
items.name_it: Finanziamento statale agli studenti DUO per cittadini UE/SEE/svizzeri/britannici
items.description: Dutch student finance for HBO/university: a basic grant, an income-tested supplementary grant and an interest-bearing loan. EU/EEA/Swiss (and UK with Article 50 document) students qualify only via work (migrant worker), a working parent/partner, or 5 consecutive years of residence in the Netherlands. Basic and supplementary grant and travel product become a gift only if you graduate within 10 years; otherwise they are a loan.

eligibility.min_work_hours: norm: at least 32 hours/month of paid work in NL; 24–32 hours/month assessed individually (24 h/month average enough after 6+ months of work); under 24 h/month not eligible unless you prove migrant-worker status
eligibility.income_test: alternative work test: earnings of at least 50% of the social security norm, € 700.75/month (2026; € 173 if under 21, as stated by DUO)
eligibility.residence_requirement: alternative to work: 5 or more consecutive years of residence in the Netherlands
other: must be younger than 30 on the day student finance starts
full-time or dual HBO/university bachelor, master or associate degree
no student finance from another country
parent or partner who is an EU/EEA/Swiss/UK migrant worker also qualifies you
UK nationals need an Article 50 TEU residence document

items.amount: Sep–Dec 2026, HBO/university, per month: basic grant € 324.52 (living away) or € 130.21 (living with parents); supplementary grant up to € 491.08; loan up to € 315.17; tuition fee loan € 224.50. Loan interest 2.33% (2026, 35-year system).
items.how_to_apply: Apply via Mijn DUO (DigiD needed) and send DUO the supporting documents on your work/residence; DUO can confirm eligibility on +31 50 599 77 11.
items.stackable: Combines with the student travel product, huurtoeslag and zorgtoeslag if their own conditions are met; not combinable with student finance from another country.

interpretations.hypothesis: The 24-hour route applies only after 6+ months of work (you, a parent or partner); between 24 and 32 hours DUO decides case by case, and you must work every month for the first six months.
Meeting the income threshold (50% of the social security norm) can qualify you as a migrant worker even with fewer hours; this is the income alternative to the hours test.

items.notes: Self-employed students must also show they are economically active (e.g. KvK registration). If average is 32 h, one month per calendar year may be skipped. Jan–Aug 2026 amounts were not shown on the DUO amounts page read today. In the loan phase (last 3 years for programmes of 4 years or less) the loan is up to € 1,213.95/month.

items.name_local: Studiefinanciering — verblijfsvergunning type I t/m V
items.name_it: Finanziamento DUO per studenti extra-UE con permesso di soggiorno
items.description: Non-EU nationals can get Dutch student finance only with a qualifying residence permit: types II, III, IV or V are eligible; type I may be eligible depending on its purpose (DUO eligibility assistant). A normal student residence permit is a type I permit. Holders of Ukrainian temporary protection are not eligible.

other: residence permit type II, III, IV or V; type I only for certain purposes
full-time or dual HBO/university programme
if awaiting a permit, apply and contact DUO within 6 weeks of receiving it for retroactive funding

items.amount: Same amounts as nl-duo-student-finance-eu when eligible.
items.how_to_apply: Check with the DUO eligibility assistant (type I) and apply via Mijn DUO.

interpretations.hypothesis: A student holding only the IND study permit (type I, temporary regular) is generally not eligible, because study is not one of the special type I purposes; only the DUO eligibility assistant settles it.
Type I holders 'may be eligible' — DUO gives no list on its page and refers to the eligibility assistant.

items.notes: The first interpretation combines two facts (study permit = type I per IND; type I only 'may' qualify per DUO); the exclusion of study-purpose type I permits was not read explicitly on an official page.

items.name_it: Borsa integrativa (in base al reddito dei genitori)
items.description: Part of student finance that depends on the parents' income from two years earlier: below the threshold you get the maximum, above it a partial grant. Siblings receiving it, other school-age children and parents' own student debt raise the amount.

eligibility.income_test: parents' combined income: max grant if below € 41,500.60 (2026, based on 2024 income) or € 43,492.62 (2027, based on 2025 income) for HBO/university
other: only for students entitled to Dutch student finance (see nl-duo-student-finance-eu / -non-eu)

items.how_to_apply: Requested together with student finance in Mijn DUO.
items.stackable: Paid together with the basic grant and loan.
items.notes: Becomes a gift if you graduate within 10 years (performance-related grant; see DUO interest press release).

items.name_it: Prestito per le tasse universitarie (collegegeldkrediet)
items.description: A loan covering tuition fees, available to EU/EEA/Swiss students (and UK with Article 50 permit) even when they do not meet the nationality/residence conditions for student finance, i.e. without working in the Netherlands. Repaid with interest after studies; months used are deducted if you later become eligible for student finance.

other: under 30
full-time or dual HBO/university programme of at least one year, accredited
you pay your tuition in the Netherlands
no work requirement

items.amount: € 224.50/month (Sep–Dec 2026, statutory fee); up to € 1,122.50/month if you pay the institutional fee, never more than the fee owed
items.how_to_apply: Form 'Aanvraag collegegeldkrediet voor studenten uit EU/EER-landen' (PDF on DUO).
items.notes: Non-EU nationals are not listed as eligible on this page.

items.name_it: Contributo per l'affitto (huurtoeslag)
items.description: Monthly rent benefit for tenants of a self-contained dwelling (own lockable entrance, kitchen, toilet and, since 1 March 2024, own shower/bath) or a designated student complex. Shared rooms usually do not qualify. From 2026 there is no hard maximum rent, but the rent counted is capped.

eligibility.income_test: income limit depends on rent, age and household (no figure on the page); assets on 1 January 2026 at most € 38,479 (single) / € 76,958 (with partner)
other: registered at the rental address with the municipality
legal residence (EU/EEA/Swiss or valid residence permit)
valid rental contract, rent paid by you; short-stay contracts ('naar zijn aard van korte duur') excluded
self-contained dwelling or designated student complex

items.amount: income-dependent; rent counted up to € 932.93/month (2026); for tenants up to 21 the rent counted is capped at € 498.20/month (2026)
items.how_to_apply: Apply online at Mijn toeslagen with DigiD; answer within about 5 weeks, payment around the 20th of the month. Report address/income changes within 4 weeks.
items.notes: From 2026 service costs no longer count, only net rent (kale huur). The youth rule was lowered from 23 to 21. Registration, residence and short-stay conditions come from the Erasmus University page, not the Belastingdienst page read today. Whether student finance counts as income for the test was not verified; use the Belastingdienst proefberekening.

items.name_it: Contributo per l'assicurazione sanitaria (zorgtoeslag)
items.description: Monthly contribution towards the Dutch basic health insurance premium. Foreign students can get it only if they must have Dutch insurance, i.e. with a paid job or an internship paid at least the minimum wage; students who only study (EHIC, home or private insurance) are not entitled.

eligibility.min_work_hours: a paid job or internship paid at least the minimum wage (no minimum hours stated)
eligibility.income_test: yearly income at most € 40,857 (single) or € 51,142 with a toeslagpartner (2026); assets at most € 146,011 (single) / € 184,633 (with partner) (2026)
other: own Dutch basic health insurance (basisverzekering)
residence permit and BSN (per UvA)

items.amount: income-dependent; the official 2026 maximum per month was not shown on the Belastingdienst pages read
items.how_to_apply: Apply online at Mijn toeslagen with DigiD after taking Dutch health insurance.
items.stackable: Combinable with huurtoeslag and student finance.

items.name_it: Abbonamento studenti ai trasporti pubblici (studentenreisproduct)
items.description: Free or discounted public transport (train, tram, bus, metro) across the Netherlands for students entitled to student finance. Weekday subscription: free Monday 04:00–Saturday 04:00, 40% off trains / 34% off bus-tram-metro at weekends, holidays and 16 July–16 August. Weekend subscription: free Friday 12:00–Monday 04:00 and holidays, discounts on weekdays from 09:00, full fare Tue–Fri before 09:00.

other: same nationality/residence conditions as student finance (EU students: work or 5-year residence route)
full-time or dual programme; for HBO/university valid for the official programme length plus one year
not usable for study or internships abroad (a public transport allowance can be requested instead)

items.amount: value € 110.95/month (2026), € 112.15/month (2027); a gift if you graduate within 10 years, otherwise a loan repaid with interest
items.how_to_apply: Apply via Mijn DUO, choosing weekday or weekend subscription; then load it on a personal OV-chipkaart (see bureaucracy nl-transport-ov-chipkaart).
items.deadline: Stop it yourself when no longer entitled; it does not stop automatically.
items.stackable: Part of student finance; combinable with the grants and loan.
items.notes: Unauthorised use costs € 96.09 per half calendar month in the first month, then € 192.21 per half calendar month (2026). Switching subscription type is possible up to twice a year. Night buses and Thalys/Eurostar are not covered; Intercity Direct needs a surcharge.

items.name_it: Dichiarazione dei redditi per studenti che lavorano
items.description: Working students pay income tax on their total income and should file an annual income tax return; the employer withholds wage tax and social security contributions. Whether and how much tax can be refunded was not verified on an official page.

other: has a paid job in the Netherlands

items.how_to_apply: File the annual income tax return (aangifte); help via employer HR or the Belastingdienst (0800 0543).
items.notes: Source is a Maastricht University page, not the Belastingdienst; the UM page also states that study grants count as taxable income, which was not confirmed officially. Loonheffingskorting and refunds were not checked.

items.name_it: Nessun limite di guadagno per chi riceve la studiefinanciering
items.description: Since 2020 students receiving Dutch student finance can earn an unlimited amount from side jobs; there is no earnings limit. For EU/EEA/Swiss students the side job is often what makes them eligible (see nl-duo-student-finance-eu).

other: receives Dutch student finance

items.stackable: Applies on top of all student finance components.

items.name_local: Studiefinanciering behouden tijdens stage of uitwisseling in het buitenland
items.name_it: Mantenere la studiefinanciering durante un Erasmus/tirocinio all'estero
items.description: Degree students at a Dutch institution who receive student finance usually keep it during a study period or internship abroad that is part of (or earns credits in) their Dutch programme. The travel product cannot be used abroad; a public transport allowance can be requested instead.

other: remains enrolled in the Dutch programme
receives student finance in the month before leaving
time abroad is part of the Dutch programme

items.how_to_apply: Nothing extra for the grant; request the public transport allowance via DUO.
items.stackable: Combinable with an Erasmus+ grant via the Dutch institution (amount not verified).
items.notes: Incoming exchange students to the Netherlands are funded by their home country's Erasmus+ grant; no Dutch host-side top-up was found. The 'stackable' claim about Erasmus+ is an inference.

items.name_it: Borsa Erasmus+ per studenti iscritti in un'università olandese
items.description: Degree students enrolled at a Dutch institution who go abroad on Erasmus+ get the grant through their Dutch institution at Dutch rates; there is also a top-up for participants with additional support needs. Monthly amounts were not found on the pages read.

other: enrolled at a Dutch higher education institution, going abroad

items.how_to_apply: Via the international office of the Dutch institution.
items.notes: Rates, and the statement that the grant is paid by the Dutch institution, are not confirmed on the page read; contact info@erasmusplus.nl / +31 70 4260 260 or the university.

items.name_it: Integrazione comunale per studenti con disabilità (individuele studietoeslag)
items.description: Municipal supplement under the Participatiewet aimed at students with a disability; conditions and amounts are set per municipality. Could not be verified on any official page today.

other: conditions not verified

items.how_to_apply: Ask the municipality where you are registered.
items.notes: Lead to verify: municipal pages (Groningen 403, Rotterdam 404) and wetten.overheid.nl (security check) could not be read.

items.name_it: NL Scholarship (ex Holland Scholarship)
items.authority: Ministry of Education (OCW) / Nuffic, with participating institutions
items.description: One-off € 5,000 in the first year for non-EEA students starting a full-time bachelor's or master's at a participating institution; not a full-tuition scholarship. Research universities participating for 2027-2028 include TU Eindhoven, Maastricht, Groningen, Twente, Utrecht, VU Amsterdam and Wageningen (not UvA, Erasmus, TU Delft, Leiden or Tilburg in that list).

other: non-EEA nationality (VU adds: Suriname and Switzerland excluded)
no previous degree from a Dutch institution
each institution sets programme levels and extra criteria (several only for master's)

items.how_to_apply: Through the participating institution's own scholarship page; deadlines per institution.
items.deadline: per institution (e.g. VU 1 February 2027; UT 1 April 2027; WUR 1 May 2027)
items.stackable: At WUR up to three awards (max € 15,000); otherwise not stated.

items.name_local: UM NL scholarships (High Potential, Brightlands Talent, Global Studies, Social Justice)
items.name_it: Borse Maastricht University per studenti extra-UE
items.description: Four UM scholarships for non-EU/EEA students in 2027/28, assessed on excellence, engagement, active citizenship and financial need. Only the UM NL Global Studies Scholarship is for a bachelor's (Global Studies); the others are for master's. Apply to a UM programme first; one scholarship application only.

other: bachelor: Global Studies only; others master's

items.how_to_apply: Apply to the programme, then via the UM scholarship application.
items.deadline: applications 1 October 2026 – 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET); complete admission file by 10 December 2026
items.notes: Award amounts are not stated on the page.

items.name_it: Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (UvA)
items.description: UvA-wide scholarship for outstanding students from outside the EU/EEA; the UvA bachelor's scholarship page lists it for exceptionally talented bachelor's applicants from outside Europe, the master's page for master's students. Amount and deadline depend on the faculty.
items.how_to_apply: Via the faculty/graduate school page of your programme.
items.notes: Amounts not stated on the pages read.

items.name_it: VU Fellowship Programme (VU Amsterdam)
items.description: Tuition fee waiver (no living costs) for non-EU/EEA students paying the higher fee, with a GPA equivalent to a Dutch 8, admitted to a full-time English-taught master's starting September 2027. VU states there are currently no scholarships for incoming bachelor's students.

other: master's only
no Dutch degree, not currently enrolled in a Dutch programme

items.how_to_apply: Apply for VUFP with the master's application (also counts as NL Scholarship application).
items.stackable: Can be combined with the NL Scholarship (€ 5,000, about 20–25 per year).

full-time enrolment at EUR during payment months
report the delay to a student counsellor
